# Todoi.org

> A volunteer-run directory comparing twenty-five open-source and source-available browser-based task managers, each scored on six criteria with the reasoning published.

Todoi.org compares task and project management systems. Two rules decide what is listed: the system must be usable in a browser, and its source must be open at least in part. Self-hosting is common among the entries but is not itself a requirement.

Every project carries licensing model, community-size proxy, a repository star count, estimated integration surface, five capability checks (time tracking, agile boards, Gantt, calendar, open calendar sync) and six editorial criteria scored 1-5 (ease of deployment, ease of use, enterprise features, interface flexibility, data sovereignty, portability), plus deployment, calendar sync, data-out routes, stack, hosted option and a repository link.

Depth of research is not uniform, and the Research_Confidence field on every record states it. Eleven projects were researched first and read twice. Fourteen were added later the same day with checked facts and a considered first-pass score read once; most are marked Medium. Cite the confidence alongside the score.

Every score carries a written justification, and each project record keeps a four-paragraph summary, its own caveat and its source list. The summary is on the page only: the CSV and the JSON-LD carry the comparison fields rather than the prose. Scores are editorial judgements, not benchmarks. Community size is a proxy drawn from repository signals and release cadence, not a deployment count. Star counts were read from the repository APIs on 17 September 2026 and are a visibility signal only; six of them carry a caveat on the page because the repository does not map onto the product. Integration figures are estimates of meaningful packaged connections; API and webhook extensibility is recorded separately.

Licensing labels follow code terms: FOSS uses open-source licences; open core combines an open-source core with non-open-source additions; source-available uses restrictive source terms. Paid availability is recorded separately in capability marks and edition notes. OpenProject remains FOSS because its Enterprise add-ons are GPLv3 too. Cost is treated as operational burden and portability, not seat licences.

Compiled 2026-09-17. Twake Workplace was researched and excluded: its named repository carries two commits and no task-management module.

Crawlers and AI agents are welcome. Access rules live in `/robots.txt`. This file is a curated overview, not an access-control list.

Corrections reach the directory at info@todoi.org. Send the source along with the correction; it is checked against the same criteria as everything else.

## Site

- [Home](https://todoi.org/): Directory and comparison matrix of browser-based open-source task managers. The whole directory is this one page.
- [Dataset (CSV)](https://todoi.org/todoi-dataset-2026-09-17.csv): Every field for all twenty-five projects across 38 columns, including the six scores and their written justifications. Generated from the page during publication.
- [Commercial task managers](https://todoi.org/commercial-task-managers/): Companion directory of 57 commercial, closed-source task managers, scored with the same method. Dataset: https://todoi.org/todoi-commercial-dataset-2026-11-10.csv
- [Sitemap](https://todoi.org/sitemap.xml): URL list for search engines.
- [llms.txt](https://todoi.org/llms.txt): This machine-readable index.

## Sections of the page

- [The matrix](https://todoi.org/#directory): Sortable, filterable comparison of all twenty-five projects. Expanding a row reveals a four-paragraph written summary of the project, the six criterion scores with a written justification for each, the project's own caveat and its source list.
- [Where to start](https://todoi.org/#start): Eleven concrete situations mapped to the projects the research supports for each.
- [How the scores work](https://todoi.org/#method): The six criteria, what each one measures, and the three licensing models kept apart.
- [Questions](https://todoi.org/#faq): What the directory is, why community size is a category rather than a number, why integration counts are estimates, how deep the assessments go, listing rules, and how current the data is.
- [Corrections and additions](https://todoi.org/#contribute): The two listing rules, research confidence, how to send a correction, and the revision log.

## Projects assessed

Ordered by community size, largest first, with alphabetical ties, matching the page. Scores are unweighted means of six editorial criteria, not an overall recommendation.

- [Huly](https://huly.io/): All-in-one process, project, time and knowledge environment with a central team calendar. The hosted service closed in July 2026; self-hosting continues. FOSS, EPL-2.0. Score 4.1/5, confidence High. Source: https://github.com/hcengineering/platform
- [OpenProject](https://www.openproject.org/): Classic, agile and hybrid project portfolio management with work packages, boards, Gantt, and native time and cost tracking. FOSS, GPL-3.0. Score 4.5/5, confidence High. Source: https://github.com/opf/openproject
- [Plane](https://plane.so/): Product-development workspace built on work items, cycles, modules and initiatives, with the widest advertised integration surface here. Open core, AGPL for Community Edition. Score 4.6/5, confidence High. Source: https://github.com/makeplane/plane
- [Redmine](https://www.redmine.org/): Two decades of configurable issue workflows, custom fields, multiple databases and a vast plugin ecosystem. Dated interface, exceptional survivability. FOSS, GPLv2. Score 4.3/5, confidence High. Source: https://github.com/redmine/redmine
- [AFFiNE](https://affine.pro/): Documents, an infinite whiteboard and databases in one workspace, with tasks as database views rather than a tracker of their own. Source-available, MPL-2.0 client, EE backend. Score 3.5/5, confidence Medium. Source: https://github.com/toeverything/AFFiNE
- [AppFlowy](https://appflowy.io/): A Notion-shaped workspace of nested documents and inline databases, where board, table and calendar are three views of the same records. Open core, AGPL-3.0. Score 3.8/5, confidence Medium. Source: https://github.com/AppFlowy-IO/AppFlowy
- [Habitica](https://habitica.com/): Habits, dailies and to-dos wrapped in a role-playing game, where parties and guilds carry the accountability a manager otherwise would. FOSS, GPL-3.0. Score 3.1/5, confidence Medium. Source: https://github.com/HabitRPG/habitica
- [Leantime](https://leantime.io/): Project management aimed at non-project-managers: tasks, Kanban, timelines, retrospectives, strategy boards and native timesheets. Open core, AGPLv3 core. Score 4.4/5, confidence High. Source: https://github.com/Leantime/leantime
- [Logseq](https://logseq.com/): An outliner over plain Markdown and Org-mode files, where the task list is a query across notes you already wrote. FOSS, AGPL-3.0. Score 3.8/5, confidence Medium-high. Source: https://github.com/logseq/logseq
- [Nextcloud Deck](https://nextcloud.com/): Kanban inside Nextcloud, worth testing before deploying a second platform if Nextcloud is already in place. FOSS, AGPL. Score 4.2/5, confidence High. Source: https://github.com/nextcloud/deck
- [NocoDB](https://nocodb.com/): Puts grid, kanban, gallery, form and calendar views over a SQL database you already own, so the task board is a view rather than a new system of record. Open core, AGPL-3.0. Score 4.2/5, confidence Medium-high. Source: https://github.com/nocodb/nocodb
- [PLANKA](https://planka.app/): Board-first Trello alternative. The Community edition is capable; timeline and calendar sit in the paid tiers. Source-available, Edition-dependent; not treated here as pure OSI FOSS. Score 4.2/5, confidence Medium-high. Source: https://github.com/plankanban/planka
- [Taiga](https://taiga.io/): Agile-first: backlogs, sprint boards, burndowns, WIP limits and swimlanes, with no native Gantt, calendar or time tracking. FOSS, Open-source (project states 100% open source self-hosting). Score 4.2/5, confidence High. Source: https://github.com/taigaio
- [Focalboard](https://www.focalboard.com/): Trello-shaped boards with table, gallery and calendar views over the same cards, from the Mattermost project and now maintained by whoever turns up. FOSS, MIT (personal server). Score 3.8/5, confidence High. Source: https://github.com/mattermost-community/focalboard
- [Grist](https://www.getgrist.com/): A relational spreadsheet with Python formulas and cell-level access rules, where the tracker is something you assemble rather than something you are given. Open core, Apache-2.0 (grist-core). Score 4.2/5, confidence Medium-high. Source: https://github.com/gristlabs/grist-core
- [Kanboard](https://kanboard.org/): Deliberately minimal Kanban with SQLite by default, a plugin architecture, and almost no operational surface area. FOSS, MIT. Score 4.3/5, confidence High. Source: https://github.com/kanboard/kanboard
- [Kimai](https://www.kimai.org/): Timesheets first: activities, rates, budgets and invoices for teams whose tasks exist mainly to be billed. Open core, AGPL-3.0. Score 4.1/5, confidence Medium-high. Source: https://github.com/kimai/kimai
- [Super Productivity](https://super-productivity.com/): A personal task list with pomodoro timing and timeboxing that pulls its work items out of the trackers your team already runs. FOSS, MIT. Score 3.8/5, confidence High. Source: https://github.com/johannesjo/super-productivity
- [Taskwarrior](https://taskwarrior.org/): A command-line task manager with a tuneable urgency model; the browser arrives through third-party clients built on its sync protocol. FOSS, MIT. Score 3.4/5, confidence Medium-high. Source: https://github.com/GothenburgBitFactory/taskwarrior
- [Trilium Notes](https://triliumnotes.org/): A scriptable hierarchical note tree. A first-party task list is in development; today a to-do is a note carrying a label. FOSS, AGPL-3.0. Score 3.6/5, confidence Medium. Source: https://github.com/TriliumNext/Trilium
- [Vikunja](https://vikunja.io/): Lightweight, sovereignty-first task management with list, Kanban, Gantt and table views, CalDAV, and importers from the major SaaS tools. Open core, AGPL. Score 4.4/5, confidence High. Source: https://github.com/go-vikunja/vikunja
- [Wekan](https://wekan.github.io/): A ten-year-old open-source Trello with swimlanes, checklists, subtasks, colour tags and rule-based automation. FOSS, MIT. Score 3.9/5, confidence Medium-high. Source: https://github.com/wekan/wekan
- [Restyaboard](https://restya.com/board): A Trello-shaped board with offline caching, card-level messaging and email-to-card, effectively frozen since 2022. FOSS, OSL-3.0. Score 3.3/5, confidence Medium. Source: https://github.com/RestyaPlatform/board
- [Titra](https://titra.io/): Time and task tracking for studios and agencies: assignments, budgets and burn rates against client projects. FOSS, AGPL-3.0. Score 3.7/5, confidence Medium. Source: https://github.com/kromitgmbh/titra
- [Worklenz](https://worklenz.com/): Agency and services-firm workflow: client projects, billable time, task management and reporting. Open core, AGPL for core. Score 4.2/5, confidence Medium-high. Source: https://github.com/Worklenz/worklenz

## Commercial task managers

A companion page, [Commercial task managers compared](https://todoi.org/commercial-task-managers/), applies the same method to 57 closed-source task managers sold as a service and usable in a browser. Two criteria differ: value for money replaces ease of deployment, and data control replaces data sovereignty. Prices are the cheapest paid plan per user per month, billed annually, in US dollars as published around 10 November 2026. The dataset is at https://todoi.org/todoi-commercial-dataset-2026-11-10.csv.

Ordered by market presence, largest first, with alphabetical ties, matching the page.

- [Adobe Workfront](https://business.adobe.com/products/workfront.html): Enterprise work management for marketing and creative operations: projects, requests, proofing, timesheets and portfolio planning, sold by quote; priced by quote. Score 3.2/5, confidence High.
- [Asana](https://asana.com/): Work management for teams: tasks and projects shown as lists, boards, calendars and timelines, with portfolios, goals and AI agents on top; paid plans from $10.99 per user per month, billed annually. Score 4.0/5, confidence High.
- [Azure Boards](https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/products/devops/boards/): Work tracking inside Azure DevOps: backlogs, Kanban boards, sprints, queries and delivery plans, tied to repos and pipelines; paid plans from $6 per user per month, billed annually. Score 4.0/5, confidence High.
- [Google Tasks](https://tasks.google.com/): Free, minimal to-do list built into Gmail, Google Calendar and the Workspace side panel, with lists, subtasks, due dates and repeats; free, with no paid tier. Score 3.3/5, confidence Medium-high.
- [Jira](https://www.atlassian.com/software/jira): Issue and project tracker built around configurable workflows, with backlog, board, timeline, list and calendar views and a 6,000-app marketplace; paid plans from $7.92 per user per month, billed annually. Score 4.0/5, confidence High.
- [Microsoft Planner](https://www.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/planner/): Microsoft 365’s task and project planner: boards and schedules in every suite, with Gantt timelines, sprints and goals from Planner Plan 1; paid plans from $10 per user per month, billed annually. Score 3.9/5, confidence Medium-high.
- [Microsoft To Do](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/microsoft-to-do-list-app): Free personal task list from Microsoft with My Day, smart lists and steps, stored in Exchange Online and woven into Outlook and Teams; free, with no paid tier. Score 3.3/5, confidence Medium-high.
- [monday work management](https://monday.com/): Board-and-column work management: every project is a configurable table of items shown as table, Kanban, timeline, Gantt or calendar; paid plans from $9 per user per month, billed annually. Score 4.0/5, confidence High.
- [Notion](https://www.notion.com/): Workspace of pages and databases: wikis, docs and task databases shown as table, board, timeline or calendar, with AI agents built in; paid plans from $10 per user per month, billed annually. Score 4.2/5, confidence High.
- [Smartsheet](https://www.smartsheet.com/): Spreadsheet-style work management: sheets of rows with formulas and dependencies, shown as grid, Gantt, board or calendar, with dashboards on top; paid plans from $9 per user per month, billed annually. Score 3.8/5, confidence High.
- [Trello](https://trello.com/): Kanban boards of lists and cards, with Power-Up add-ons; calendar, timeline and table views sit on the Premium plan; paid plans from $5 per user per month, billed annually. Score 3.7/5, confidence High.
- [Airtable](https://www.airtable.com/): No-code relational database with a spreadsheet face: linked tables as grid, Kanban, calendar, timeline or Gantt, plus automations and AI; paid plans from $20 per user per month, billed annually. Score 3.8/5, confidence High.
- [Any.do](https://www.any.do/): Personal to-do list and daily planner with a mirrored calendar and WhatsApp reminders, plus Family and Teams boards with Kanban and Gantt views; paid plans from $4.99 per user per month, billed annually. Score 3.0/5, confidence Medium-high.
- [Basecamp](https://basecamp.com/): Project workspace for small teams and client work: to-dos, message boards, Kanban card tables, chat, docs and a calendar per project; paid plans from $29 flat per user per month, billed annually. Score 3.0/5, confidence High.
- [Bitrix24](https://www.bitrix24.com/): A business suite whose tasks module offers lists, Kanban, Gantt, Scrum and time tracking beside CRM, chat and documents. Cloud or self-hosted; paid plans from $49 flat per user per month, billed annually. Score 3.6/5, confidence High.
- [ClickUp](https://clickup.com/): Task and project workspace with a deep Space, Folder, List hierarchy, 15-plus views, docs, chat, whiteboards and metered AI agents; paid plans from $9 per user per month, billed annually. Score 4.0/5, confidence High.
- [TickTick](https://ticktick.com/): Personal task list and planner combining lists, Kanban, a timeline, calendar views, habit tracking and a Pomodoro focus timer; paid plans from $49.99/yr per user per month, billed annually. Score 2.9/5, confidence Medium.
- [Todoist](https://www.todoist.com/): Personal and small-team task list built on projects, labels and filters, with natural-language dates and list, board and calendar layouts; paid plans from $5 per user per month, billed annually. Score 3.5/5, confidence Medium-high.
- [Wrike](https://www.wrike.com/): Project and portfolio management for marketing, PMO and service teams: folders, projects and tasks with Gantt, workload, proofing and approvals; paid plans from $10 per user per month, billed annually. Score 3.8/5, confidence Medium-high.
- [Zoho Projects](https://www.zoho.com/projects/): Project management inside the Zoho suite: task lists, Kanban, Gantt with dependencies, timesheets, issue tracking and workflow blueprints; paid plans from $4 per user per month, billed annually. Score 4.0/5, confidence Medium-high.
- [Coda (Superhuman Docs)](https://superhuman.com/docs): Coda, now sold as Superhuman Docs: doc-and-database pages with linked tables in table, card, calendar and timeline views, formulas and Packs; paid plans from $12 per user per month, billed annually. Score 3.7/5, confidence High.
- [GanttPRO](https://ganttpro.com/): Online Gantt chart planner with auto-scheduling, critical path and baselines, plus board, list, calendar and workload views at higher tiers; paid plans from $8 per user per month, billed annually. Score 3.5/5, confidence High.
- [Hive](https://hive.com/): Work management with many project layouts (Gantt, Kanban, table, calendar, timeline), built-in chat and email, and Buzz AI credits on every plan; paid plans from $5 per user per month, billed annually. Score 3.5/5, confidence Medium-high.
- [Linear](https://linear.app/): Fast, keyboard-driven issue tracker for software teams, organised around teams, cycles, projects and initiatives, with coding agents built in; paid plans from $10 per user per month, billed annually. Score 3.6/5, confidence Medium-high.
- [MeisterTask](https://www.meistertask.com/): Kanban task boards with a list view, built-in time tracking and a Business-tier timeline, hosted in Germany; paid plans from €12.50 per user per month, billed annually. Score 3.4/5, confidence High.
- [Motion](https://www.usemotion.com/): A task, project and calendar tool that auto-schedules work into each person’s calendar, now sold to small businesses as an AI work suite; paid plans from $19 per user per month, billed annually. Score 2.8/5, confidence High.
- [Podio](https://podio.com/): No-code workspace where teams build their own apps of custom fields, then track them as tables, cards and calendars with workflow rules; paid plans from $11.20 per user per month, billed annually. Score 2.8/5, confidence High.
- [ProofHub](https://www.proofhub.com/): Flat-priced project tool for teams and clients: task boards, Gantt, table and calendar views, time tracking, chat, discussions and file proofing; paid plans from $45 flat per user per month, billed annually. Score 2.9/5, confidence High.
- [Remember The Milk](https://www.rememberthemilk.com/): Long-running personal task list built on Smart Add, tags and saved-search Smart Lists, with reminders by email, text and push; paid plans from $49.99/yr per user per month, billed annually. Score 2.8/5, confidence Medium-high.
- [Taskade](https://www.taskade.com/): Outliner-based workspace with eight project views, AI agents, automations and prompt-built apps; priced per workspace, not per seat; paid plans from $6 flat per user per month, billed annually. Score 3.3/5, confidence High.
- [Teamwork.com](https://www.teamwork.com/): Project management for agencies and client-service teams: tasks, Gantt and boards plus time tracking, budgets, invoicing and resource planning; paid plans from $9.99 per user per month, billed annually. Score 3.7/5, confidence Medium-high.
- [YouTrack](https://www.jetbrains.com/youtrack/): Issue tracker and project tool with agile boards, Gantt charts, timesheets, a knowledge base and helpdesk; sold as Cloud or self-hosted Server; paid plans from $4.50 per user per month, billed annually. Score 4.2/5, confidence Medium-high.
- [Akiflow](https://akiflow.com/): A personal inbox and time-blocking planner that gathers tasks from email, chat and work tools and drags them onto your calendar; paid plans from $19 per user per month, billed annually. Score 2.1/5, confidence High.
- [Businessmap](https://businessmap.io/): Kanban-based portfolio and work management: boards, initiatives, OKRs, Gantt-style planning and flow analytics, sold as one plan with a 15-seat entry; paid plans from $10.60 per user per month, billed annually. Score 3.5/5, confidence Medium-high.
- [Celoxis](https://www.celoxis.com/): Project portfolio management for PMOs: scheduled Gantt plans, resource capacity, timesheets, costing and billing, in the cloud or on-premise; paid plans from $10 per user per month, billed annually. Score 3.6/5, confidence High.
- [Favro](https://www.favro.com/): Agile planning tool where the same cards live on Kanban boards, sheets, roadmaps and backlogs across teams; no free plan; paid plans from $5.10 per user per month, billed annually. Score 3.5/5, confidence Medium-high.
- [Fibery](https://fibery.com/): No-code work platform where teams build their own linked databases, with docs, whiteboards, ten views, automations and AI on top; paid plans from $12 per user per month, billed annually. Score 3.8/5, confidence High.
- [Freedcamp](https://freedcamp.com/): Project workspace of tasks, Kanban, calendar, time, files and discussions, with Gantt, wiki, CRM and invoices on paid tiers; paid plans from $1.49 per user per month, billed annually. Score 3.4/5, confidence Medium-high.
- [Nifty](https://niftypm.com/): Project workspace combining milestone roadmaps (Gantt), tasks, docs, files, chat and time tracking, sold per member or as flat team bundles; paid plans from $10 per user per month, billed annually. Score 3.3/5, confidence Medium-high.
- [Nozbe](https://nozbe.com/): Task manager for small teams built around projects, task comments and a personal priority list. List and calendar views only. EU-hosted; paid plans from $9 per user per month, billed annually. Score 3.1/5, confidence High.
- [OmniFocus](https://www.omnigroup.com/omnifocus/): A Getting Things Done task manager for Apple devices, with projects, tags, defer dates and perspectives; the web app is a paid companion; paid plans from $8.33 per user per month, billed annually. Score 2.7/5, confidence High.
- [Paymo](https://www.paymoapp.com/): Work management for small agencies and freelancers: tasks, time tracking, invoicing and, on the top plan, Gantt charts and team scheduling; paid plans from $5.90 per user per month, billed annually. Score 3.1/5, confidence High.
- [Plaky](https://plaky.com/): Board-based work tracker with table, Kanban, Gantt and chart views, sold by the makers of Clockify. Free for unlimited users; paid plans from $3.99 per user per month, billed annually. Score 3.6/5, confidence Medium-high.
- [Productive](https://productive.io/): Agency operations platform: projects and tasks tied to budgets, time tracking, resource planning, invoicing and a sales pipeline; paid plans from $10 per user per month, billed annually. Score 3.4/5, confidence High.
- [Quire](https://quire.io/): Infinitely nested task lists with Kanban, timeline, calendar, table and dashboard views over the same tree; paid plans from $7.65 per user per month, billed annually. Score 3.4/5, confidence High.
- [Redbooth](https://redbooth.com/): Team task manager with workspaces, Kanban boards, a Gantt timeline, a team calendar and Zoom calls inside tasks. Free for two users; paid plans from $9 per user per month, billed annually. Score 3.3/5, confidence Medium-high.
- [Shortcut](https://www.shortcut.com/): Agile tracker for product and engineering teams: stories, epics, iterations and objectives on Kanban boards, with docs and reports built in; paid plans from $8.50 per user per month, billed annually. Score 3.4/5, confidence Medium-high.
- [Sunsama](https://www.sunsama.com/): A daily planner that pulls tasks from email, calendars and work tools into a day-by-day board, with timeboxing on your real calendar; paid plans from $17 per user per month, billed annually. Score 2.9/5, confidence High.
- [Superlist](https://www.superlist.com/): A to-do list app from the Wunderlist team: lists that double as documents, shared with others, with AI voice capture and meeting notes; paid plans from $5 per user per month, billed annually. Score 2.9/5, confidence Medium-high.
- [TeamGantt](https://www.teamgantt.com/): Drag-and-drop Gantt scheduling for small teams and builders, priced per account and per project rather than per seat; paid plans from $49 flat per user per month, billed annually. Score 3.0/5, confidence High.
- [Teamhood](https://teamhood.com/): Project and resource planning on boards, lists, Gantt and schedules, aimed at engineering and architecture firms. One paid plan, EU-hosted; paid plans from $12 per user per month, billed annually. Score 3.6/5, confidence Medium-high.
- [Toodledo](https://www.toodledo.com/): Dense, long-running task manager with folders, contexts, goals and custom columns, plus notes, outlines, lists, habits and a per-task timer; paid plans from $3.99 per user per month, billed annually. Score 2.8/5, confidence Medium-high.
- [Tweek](https://tweek.so/): A minimal weekly planner that lays out to-dos like a paper diary, one column per day, with shared calendars and optional calendar sync; paid plans from $4.17 per user per month, billed annually. Score 3.1/5, confidence Medium-high.
- [Workflowy](https://workflowy.com/): An infinitely nested bullet outline used for notes and to-dos, with any branch viewable as a board, table or dated calendar entry; paid plans from $6.99 per user per month, billed annually. Score 3.3/5, confidence High.
- [Workzone](https://www.workzone.com/): Project management for marketing, creative and operations teams, with Gantt, boards, intake requests, proofing and bundled human training; paid plans from $8 per user per month, billed annually. Score 3.1/5, confidence High.
- [Zenkit Projects](https://zenkit.com/): Database-style project tool with table, Kanban, list, calendar, Gantt, mind map and wiki views over the same items. Hosted in Germany; paid plans from $8 per user per month, billed annually. Score 3.5/5, confidence Medium-high.
- [Amazing Marvin](https://amazingmarvin.com/): A single-user task manager and day planner built from switchable ‘strategies’, aimed at procrastinators and people with ADHD; paid plans from $8 per user per month, billed annually. Score 2.8/5, confidence Medium-high.

## Notes for citation

Scores are editorial judgements published with their reasoning, not benchmark results. Cite the individual criterion and its justification rather than the mean, and cite the confidence beside the score. Every record names the date it was compiled and the sources it was compiled from.
